plan: CURRICULUM_GAME_MASTER_APPROACH.md — Stage 0 reference bars ('local routing search / bounded short-rollout search where available'), the enabler EXP-0023 flagged as the first curriculum blocker (the fixed practical bar was too weak to expose any policy gap).
question: Does a stronger, checkpoint-free reference bar (per-cycle directed short-rollout orderer search, producer fixed at entity_planner) expose in-claim policy_weakness the fixed entity_planner+proportional bar could not — so Stage 3 hard-case mining has a reference that can actually surface gaps?
scope: Reference-bar strength only. Same 18-task stress suite as EXP-0023, same portable stack (no champion change, no training, no promotion). Adds the search bar and best-of-bars reference selection; default single-bar behaviour (EXP-0023) unchanged.

stack_under_test.note: identical to EXP-0023; this experiment varies only the REFERENCE, not the learner

reference_bars.entity_planner+proportional: fixed practical bar (EXP-0023) — entity planner producer + proportional orderer, deterministic, no checkpoint
reference_bars.entity_planner+mpc_search: bounded short-rollout / directed routing search — producer fixed at entity_planner, orderer routing re-chosen each cycle by lookahead=6 rollout over {even_split, proportional} + 8 sampled routing vectors (search_orderer_episode, EXP-0005). Deterministic given seed (sample RNG seeded by seed+cycle). No checkpoint.
reference_bars.selection: reference = strongest of the enabled bars per task (max mean consumer units); winning bar id retained in reference_model_id so every row's ratio is attributable (never read against an unknown bar). Ties -> first-registered bar.
